answer: Each agent can claim only one account backed by a bonded, nontransferable credential issued after a scarce real-world check, such as an in-person liveness challenge. Rewards are capped per credential, so splitting activity across accounts does not multiply payouts. An attacker must obtain more checks and lock more capital for each extra identity, making a large sybil network costly to build and maintain. A lotus, haven, or mirror account still needs its own valid bond; changing names or copying behavior earns no additional share.
